analysis:
The PR changes documentation only: docs/provider/hardware-requirements.md (new GLM-5.3-Flash wired-memory paragraph, head lines 46-57) and docs/provider/troubleshooting.md (new `glm wired limit` doctor row, a verify exclusion note, a new troubleshooting row, and a new section after line 170). It contains no code, protocol, attestation, authorization or encryption changes. The coordinator-to-provider contract (TB-002), App Attest authorization (TB-011), A-001 and the prefix-cache threat (T-041) are untouched.

The new guidance tells operators to run `sudo sysctl -w` with fixed values (`iogpu.wired_limit_mb=245760`, `vm.global_user_wire_limit` and `vm.user_wire_limit` = 261134011596). It also tells them to install a root LaunchDaemon at `/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.layrlabs.glm53-wired-limits.plist`. The docs state the provider never runs sudo itself, so the provider gains no new privileged path and the fan-helper boundary (TB-010, T-044/T-045) is not affected. The LaunchDaemon sits in a root-owned directory and runs a fixed `/usr/sbin/sysctl -w` command, so it is not a user-writable root-execution vector like T-045. The daemon block text is produced by `GLMWiredLimitAdvice.swift`, which is not in the supplied evidence. I could not verify that the printed block uses absolute paths, root ownership or safe permissions, or that it does not interpolate untrusted data. This is an unverified contract for integration, not a finding.

Raising wired limits to about 95% of RAM is an operator availability and tuning choice. It is documented as changing no admission or capacity figure, and it does not weaken the memory load gates. I identified no regression and no invalidated threat-model assumption.
